verdict.rationale: Missive's changelog says external AI apps (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor) can connect through its MCP server and act on conversations, contacts, calendar and drafts "with the permissions you choose". That is a first-party but thin indication of permission-scoped agent access. The OAuth custom-scopes evidence (docs-68) concerns Missive authenticating outbound to third-party MCP servers, and the credential-swap note concerns AI provider keys, so neither counts toward issuing scoped credentials. Missing for 10: documentation of how API tokens are issued and scoped, the granular permission model (read/write, per-resource or per-account), token revocation and expiry, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: External AI apps like Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor can now connect to Missive through the Model Context Protocol and act on your conversations, contacts, calendar, and drafts, with the permissions you choose.
